case_title: Satyendra Kumar Mehra v. The State of Jharkhand
statutory_provisions: IPC s.120-B, s.420, s.467, s.468, s.471, s.477-A; Prevention of Corruption Act s.13(1)(c) & (d), s.13(2)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to R.I. of five years with fine of Rs.25,000/- and in default S.I. of three months
high_court_outcome: Allowed suspension of sentence and directed deposit of fine amount awarded
neutral_facts: The accused was tried for an offence punishable under sections 120-B, 420, 467, 468, 471, and 477-A of the IPC, read with sections 13(1)(c) & (d) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. The trial court convicted the accused and imposed a sentence of rigorous imprisonment for five years with a fine of Rs.25,000/- and in default, simple imprisonment for three months. The accused filed an appeal before the High Court, which allowed the suspension of the sentence and directed the accused to deposit the fine amount awarded. The accused challenged this direction, arguing that the fine should be stayed under section 357(2) of the Cr.P.C. The High Court's order was appealed to the Supreme Court.
